free_tier.stated: Free, unlimited distribution; ~1.4 million items already torrented, 'comprising almost a petabyte of public domain materials'. Egress is unbounded because the swarm and webseeds share the load.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Torrents rely heavily on webseeding: download directly from Archive servers when no peers have the files. The page states no price and no bandwidth limit for torrent or webseed download.

interface_detail: BitTorrent protocol: .torrent files per item with Getright-style webseeding, tracked by bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org
tooling: A BitTorrent client with Getright-style webseeding support; the Archive generates the .torrent per item and runs the trackers bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org.
chaining: Archive BitTorrents are made automatically for community-contributed items in many collections and updated when the item changes. The torrent falls back on webseeding from Archive servers when no peers have the files.
limits_note: Torrents become obsolete when the item changes, and some or all files then fail to download completely. Clients without Getright-style webseeding, such as rTorrent, cannot download un-seeded Archive torrents. The ._____padding_file directory should be deselected. The trackers bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org are closed and track only the Archive's own torrents. A torrent for an item without one is requested by email to info@archive.org.

identity_cost.detail: The torrent page names no account requirement for downloading. Creating the item that receives an Archive torrent needs a free archive.org account.

reliability_note: Old torrents for a mutated item loop forever re-downloading mismatched pieces; seeder counts are cached ~5 minutes and include webseeds.

extras.verified_at_basis: re-checked against the first-party page on 2026-11-19 (a verify run); evidence rows dated by the seed pass, which ended 2026-10-21, keep that date as an upper bound
extras.quota_verbatim: Free, unlimited distribution; ~1.4 million items already torrented, 'comprising almost a petabyte of public domain materials'. Egress is unbounded because the swarm and webseeds share the load.
extras.limits_verbatim: Torrent is generated server-side only (you do not choose the swarm); obsolete torrents break when the item changes (piece-hash mismatch); rTorrent does not support Getright-style webseeding and will not start; bt1 trackers are rate-limited per IP; ._____padding_file must be deselected.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free — 'our Torrents rely heavily on webseeding (download directly from our servers, when no peers have the files you are seeking)'. Peers carry the rest at zero cost to anyone.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Combine with #1: upload once via IAS3, then distribute via torrent so a 1TiB/day fetch load is carried by peers + webseed instead of a single HTTP stream. Torrent + webseed is also the only path that can exceed the ~1.7 MB/s per-connection shaping.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Any BitTorrent client with Getright-style webseed support (qBittorrent, Transmission); IA generates the .torrent per item and runs trackers bt1.archive.org; rclone not involved
extras.agent_focus: Internet Archive deep dive: IAS3 S3-like API, per-item unlimited size, upload API, metadata, derivatives, CDX, the web archive as a CDN, practical throughput/rate limits for 20TB
